summary: Birmingham City Council's planning register is NOT reachable from this environment: eplanning.birmingham.gov.uk (Northgate Planning Explorer) returns HTTP 403 to every request, and planning.birmingham.gov.uk, birmingham.gov.uk (weekly-list PDFs), planit.org.uk, landcycle.com, planningappealsuk.com and acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk are all blocked by the outbound agent proxy ("gateway answered 403 to CONNECT — policy denial"), confirmed both via WebFetch and curl with the proxy CA bundle. All findings below therefore come from Google/WebSearch result snippets of indexed portal pages, not from the portal itself. What was recoverable: (1) 2025/04397/PA — 131 Vicarage Road, Kings Heath B14 7QQ, householder application for "erection of a first floor rear extension", received in the council's weekly list for 10–16 Aug 2025; decision status not recoverable — this is the most relevant recent rear-extension precedent on the street. (2) 2015/01188/PA — 1 Vicarage Road, Kings Heath B14 7QA, change of use from offices (A2) to residential (C3), registered 12-03-2015, approved with conditions 30-04-2015. (3) An eplanning details page for 2014/06721/PA was returned by Google against a query for 111/113/117 Vicarage Road, but its content (address/description/decision) could not be retrieved — it needs checking on the portal. (4) No trace of the 2005 application S/03404/05/FUL at 115 Vicarage Road in any indexed source — old S-prefix records exist on the Northgate portal but are not Google-indexed. (5) No public trace of pre-app 2026/03356/PA — Birmingham does not generally publish pre-application advice files on the public register, so this may never appear online. (6) The neighbour anecdote ("one rejected a few doors down, then they put in high-level windows and a lantern") could not be verified without portal access. (7) Appeals: no Vicarage Road appeal found; search snippets identified a dismissed appeal at 65 Church Road, Moseley & Kings Heath B13 9EB (second-floor side extension), a Birmingham retrospective rear-extension appeal refused for breaching the 45-Degree Code (loss of light/outlook) described on planningappealsuk.com, and an acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk decision PDF (fileid=64492257) that mentions Birmingham B14 but could not be opened. Practical fallback: the register is publicly searchable at https://eplanning.birmingham.gov.uk/Northgate/PlanningExplorer/GeneralSearch.aspx from any normal browser, and pre-2010 files (incl. S/03404/05/FUL) may require a documents request to planning.enquiries@birmingham.gov.uk.

facts.detail: eplanning.birmingham.gov.uk returns HTTP 403 to all requests (search page and StdDetails pages) via both WebFetch and curl; the agent proxy log shows 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)' for planning.birmingham.gov.uk and other planning hosts. birmingham.gov.uk weekly-list PDFs, planit.org.uk API, landcycle.com, planningappealsuk.com and acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk are equally blocked. Only WebSearch snippets were usable.

Householder application: 'Erection of a first floor rear extension' at 131 Vicarage Road, Birmingham, B14 7QQ. Appears in Birmingham's weekly list of applications received 10–16 August 2025. Decision and approved dimensions not recoverable from search snippets. This is the closest recent rear-extension precedent to the target properties (105–125 range) that could be found.

facts.topic: Neighbour anecdote (rejected scheme a few doors down, then high-level windows + roof lantern)
facts.detail: Could not be verified. No refused application at 105–125 Vicarage Road surfaced in indexed weekly lists or snippets. The described redesign (high-level/obscure-glazed flank windows plus a roof lantern instead of conventional rear-facing glazing at first floor) is the classic response to a 45-Degree Code / overlooking refusal, so the account is plausible, but the actual refs need a portal address search on 'Vicarage Road' filtered to B14 7QG/7QQ.
facts.source: Absence from all accessible search results

facts.detail: planningappealsuk.com describes a Birmingham City Council appeal concerning a retrospective rear extension refused for non-compliance with the '45 Degree Code for House Extensions' and loss of outlook/light to a neighbour (page 403-blocked, details from snippet only). A dismissed appeal at 65 Church Road, Moseley & Kings Heath, B13 9EB concerned a second-floor side extension. An acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk decision document (fileid=64492257) matching 'Vicarage Road Kings Heath B14' query mentions Birmingham B14 but could not be opened. No Vicarage Road appeal decision was positively identified. Context sources confirm the 45-degree rule is the decisive daylight test Birmingham applies in Moseley/Kings Heath (B13/B14) Victorian/Edwardian terraces, measured from the centre of the nearest habitable-room window of the adjoining house.
facts.value: No Vicarage Road appeal found; 45-Degree Code confirmed as key refusal ground in B13/B14 appeals
facts.source: WebSearch snippets: planningappealsuk.com, mcternandesign.co.uk, acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk results

facts.topic: How to complete this research manually
facts.detail: From an unproxied browser: (1) eplanning.birmingham.gov.uk > Planning Applications On-Line > address search 'Vicarage Road' + Kings Heath, which lists all historic apps incl. S-prefix 2005 records; (2) appealfinder.co.uk Birmingham City Council page and acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk case search (LPA: Birmingham, keyword 'rear extension', postcodes B13/B14) for 45-degree appeal precedents; (3) weekly lists at birmingham.gov.uk/planningapplications for anything received in 2026.
facts.source: Portal structure inferred from indexed URLs
